At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ defeated rivals including HBO to become the most-awarded platform. Here is HBO's Casey Bloys's response to Apple TV+'s victory.

The HBO CEO highly praised Apple TV+'s outstanding performance, but also acknowledged that competing with a company worth a trillion dollars is "quite challenging."

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, with both prioritising quality over quantity. Apple is even sometimes called "the new HBO."

Last night's Emmys further cemented this narrative, with Apple TV+ surpassing HBO, Netflix and other platforms to become the most-awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV+ won a total of 29 awards, becoming the "most-awarded network of the year," with shows like Widow's Bay performing particularly well. HBO came in second with 21 awards.

After the Emmy Awards ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys was interviewed by Deadline and asked about his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. His response is below:

DEADLINE: What do you think of Apple TV+'s performance this time? They've become the most-awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time. How do you see it? BLOYS: Well, I'm actually quite pleased, because I think they're very formidable competitors, Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors—Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon—so with Apple, everyone keeps us on our toes, and that's when I perform at my best. They're a trillion-dollar company, which is indeed quite challenging, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best programming.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has served as head of programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s victory was largely quite gracious, with sincere congratulations offered.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a trillion-dollar company, which is indeed quite challenging."

We're not sure what Apple TV+'s internal budget is, but there's no question that Apple as a whole has vastly greater financial resources than most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does size automatically bring advantages? Perhaps. But many networks have proven that, when it comes to producing content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and is also available through the Apple One bundle subscription service.
